answer: Require each agent to post a refundable bond, then slash it when audits find duplicated control or fabricated work. Auditors compare signed task histories and sample outputs for repeated patterns; this is not proof of unique identity, but it raises the cost of operating a sybil cluster. An attacker must lock capital for every persona and risks losing the bonds if caught. The bond is an anchor, audits are the river that exposes repeated tracks, and even a sparrow-sized agent pays the same entry price.
